headline: Friday's coastal flooding winds down this afternoon after one more minor round along western Long Island Sound, then a breezy, showery Friday gives way to a quiet weekend before about a half inch of rain Sunday night into early Monday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Friday brings light rain and scattered showers around New York City as a storm passes well to the northwest through northern New York, with the best chances north and west of the city and a few showers possible this afternoon into early evening. Southwest winds gust 20 to 30 mph, strongest in the city and near the coast. Tonight winds turn more westerly and ease a bit, though gusts around 20 to 25 mph are still possible in the city, and skies are most likely to clear this evening and overnight.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday brings west winds gusting about 20 to 30 mph from mid-morning, possibly with some low clouds in the afternoon, before winds ease Saturday evening and night. Sunday looks dry and quiet. Rain returns Sunday night, most likely after midnight, as low pressure tracks from the eastern Great Lakes into northern New England, possibly with a second, smaller low crossing the area; expect about a half inch, not enough to cause flooding, with a slight chance of thunder and south winds gusting about 25 to 35 mph late Sunday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Rain may linger east of the city after sunrise Monday, but conditions improve through the day as winds swing around to the west and gust about 30 to 40 mph. Winds die down Monday night, and Tuesday and Wednesday look quiet. The discussion gives no temperature details.

coast: High tide has largely passed on Long Island's south shore and around New York Harbor, where some leftover minor flooding is possible as water recedes; the approaching high tide along western Long Island Sound (coastal Westchester, the North Shore and coastal Connecticut) brings another round of minor coastal flooding. Coastal Flood Advisories end between noon and 4 PM Friday depending on location. Beach flooding and dune erosion continue through early afternoon, with 8 to 12 foot breaking waves gradually shrinking through the day. On the water, a Gale Warning covers the ocean and a Small Craft Advisory covers the Sound, harbor and bays until 6 AM Saturday, with leftover swell making the entrances to Long Island Sound and New York Harbor rough much of Friday; small craft conditions are likely on the ocean Saturday (possibly the Sound and bays too), all waters settle below advisory levels Sunday, and gales are expected on the ocean again Sunday night into Monday, with a few gale-force gusts possible on the Sound and bays.
watch_for: Minor coastal flooding at this afternoon's high tide along western Long Island Sound
Timing of Sunday night's rain, with a slight chance of thunder and gusty winds
Gusty west winds Monday and gales returning on the ocean Sunday night into Monday
confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in today's showers and about a half inch of rain Sunday night, but less certain about a possible second low then and how much wind it brings, which for now looks minimal.
